quiz.q: You rename a Mule project in Anypoint Studio (Refactor → Rename). What happens to the artifactId in pom.xml?
options: It is renamed to match the new project name
It stays the same — you must edit pom.xml yourself
It is removed and regenerated on the next build
It becomes the API instance ID
quiz.explain: Refactor → Rename changes only the project name. The artifactId in pom.xml is unchanged, and repositories identify a project by its artifactId.

quiz.q: Two projects in your workspace have the same groupId and artifactId. What error does Studio show?
quiz.explain: Studio reports "Conflicting Maven coordinates" when two projects share groupId + artifactId.

quiz.q: Which property keys must the deployed app use so it can connect to API Manager?
quiz.explain: The keys need underscores: anypoint.platform.client_id and anypoint.platform.client_secret. Typing clientid was one of the reasons the Day 35 deployment hung.

quiz.q: Which deployment option keeps the old version running until the new one is up, so there is no downtime?
quiz.explain: Rolling update keeps the old version serving until the new version runs. Recreate kills the old one first, causing a brief gap.

quiz.q: After deploying an app whose Autodiscovery has the right API instance ID, what status does the API show in API Manager?
quiz.explain: The status changes from Unregistered to Active once the running app connects to API Manager through Autodiscovery.

quiz.q: With the Basic Authentication – Simple policy, how many sets of credentials are there?
options: One username/password shared by all consumers
One client ID and secret per consumer
quiz.explain: Basic Authentication – Simple checks a single shared username and password for every consumer.

quiz.q: A request fails the Basic Authentication policy. Where does the rejection happen?
options: In the Mule flow's error handler
At the API gateway, before the app
quiz.explain: The gateway rejects it with 401, so the request never reaches the app and doesn't appear in the app's logs.

quiz.q: How does Postman build the header for Basic Auth?
quiz.explain: The header is Authorization: Basic followed by Base64 of username:password. The word Basic must be written exactly.

quiz.q: Where does a consumer get a client ID and secret for an API protected by Client ID Enforcement?
quiz.explain: Request access in Exchange creates an application with its own client ID and secret. The secret is shown under Exchange → My applications.

quiz.q: What does API Manager create each time a consumer's request for access is approved?
quiz.explain: Each request for access creates a contract in API Manager — the record of that application's approved access.

quiz.q: What error does Client ID Enforcement return for a wrong or missing client ID?
quiz.explain: A wrong or missing client ID/secret returns 401 with "Invalid Client".

quiz.q: In the class demo, the custom-expression headers were renamed. What must the consumer do?
options: Send the headers exactly as defined in the policy (c_id / c_secret)
quiz.explain: The policy reads credentials from the expression you configure, so consumers must send exactly those header names — c_id and c_secret in the demo.

cards.back: The project's unique ID in Maven and repositories, in pom.xml — separate from the display name. Renaming a project does not change it.
Studio error when two projects share the same groupId + artifactId.

cards.front: Property keys for connecting a deployed app to API Manager
cards.back: anypoint.platform.client_id and anypoint.platform.client_secret (with underscores) — the organization's credentials from Access Management.
Rolling update: old version keeps running until the new one is up — no downtime. Recreate: old version is killed first — brief downtime.
API Manager status changes to Active once a deployed app with that API instance ID connects through Autodiscovery.
Policy that checks one username/password shared by all consumers.
Policy that checks a client ID and secret per consumer, so you know who called and can revoke one consumer.

cards.front: Where do client ID and secret come from?
cards.back: Exchange → Request access creates an application with its own ID/secret; the secret is under Exchange → My applications.
The record of an application's approved access to an API — one is created for each request for access.

cards.front: How can consumers send client credentials?
cards.back: As HTTP Basic (ID as username, secret as password) or in custom headers defined by the policy's expression, e.g. client_id / client_secret.

cards.front: Does a request rejected by a policy reach the Mule app?
cards.back: No — the gateway rejects it (401), so it doesn't appear in the app's logs.
Authorization: Basic <Base64(username:password)> — the word Basic must be written exactly.

cards.back: Wrong property keys (clientid), stray digits in the API instance ID, and an app name clashing with an Exchange asset — fixed by renaming the project and its artifactId.
